name: Runner AI
tagline: An AI agent product that takes a natural language instruction and runs the multi-step work for you.

pricing.notes: AI-drafted from a site submission; price unverified.

verdictSummary: The shape of this category is well understood: an LLM in a loop, a set of tools, a browser or shell it can drive, and a log of what it did. A coding agent will hand you that in a session, and for narrow repeatable tasks your version will work fine. What it will not hand you is the boring 80 percent: retries that actually recover, sane handling of logins and two-factor prompts, cost ceilings, and the judgment to stop instead of confidently doing the wrong thing twice. You also inherit a hard dependency on somebody's model API, so this is not self-contained in any meaningful sense. Build it if you want a scriptable agent for your own five workflows, not if you want something you would trust unattended.
coreLoopDIY: A local CLI that takes a plain-English task, drives a real browser through an LLM tool-use loop, and writes a step-by-step transcript you can audit.
requirements: An LLM API key with a real spend limit set
Node 20+ and Playwright browsers installed locally
Patience for prompt tuning, the first ten runs will be bad
Your own credentials in .env for any site the agent touches
whatYouLose: Reliability engineering: the failure modes are endless and yours will hit all of them
Any hosted schedule or trigger, your agent only runs when your laptop is awake
Prebuilt integrations and auth flows for common services
Guardrails and approval UX that stop an agent mid-mistake
Someone else eating the token bill and tuning the model choice for you
moatNotes: Nobody in this space owns the model. The differentiation is harness quality, tool coverage, and how gracefully the thing fails.
whyPeopleStillPay: Because an agent that works 70 percent of the time is worse than no agent, and closing that last 30 percent is unglamorous full-time work. Paid products absorb the retry logic, the browser fingerprinting fights, the session storage, the scheduling, and the model churn every few months. They also give you a place to click cancel when the agent starts filling in the wrong form. A local loop is genuinely useful for tasks you supervise; it stops being useful the moment you want to walk away from the screen.
notes: The demo will feel like magic and the eleventh run will feel like debugging someone else's intern.
prompt:
Build a local, single-user AI task runner as a CLI. No web UI, no accounts, no telemetry, no cloud.

Stack, non-negotiable: TypeScript, Node 20, Playwright (Chromium, headed by default), Anthropic Messages API with tool use, better-sqlite3 for run history, commander for the CLI. No frameworks beyond that.

Commands:
- `runner do "task text"` : start a new run
- `runner runs` : list past runs with status, step count, token cost
- `runner show <id>` : print the full transcript of a run
- `runner replay <id>` : re-run the same task text

Core loop: send the task plus current page state to the model, receive a tool call, execute it, append the result, repeat until the model returns a final answer or the step cap (default 30) is hit.

Tools to expose: navigate(url), click(selector_or_text), type(selector, text), read_page() returning trimmed visible text plus a numbered list of interactive elements, screenshot() returning a base64 image, wait(ms), run_shell(cmd), finish(summary).

Safety, implement properly, do not stub:
- A confirm gate: any run_shell call, any click on text matching /delete|pay|submit|buy|send/i, and any navigation off the allowlist prompts the user in the terminal for y/n.
- ALLOWED_DOMAINS in .env, comma separated. Navigation outside it requires confirmation.
- A hard USD cost ceiling per run from .env; abort with a clear message when exceeded.
- Persist a browser profile directory so logins survive between runs. Never write credentials into the SQLite DB or the transcript; redact anything typed into a field whose selector or label matches /pass|token|secret|otp|code/i.

Write every step to SQLite: run id, timestamp, tool name, arguments, truncated result, tokens in/out. Save screenshots to ./runs/<id>/ as PNGs and reference them in the transcript.

Secrets in .env only: ANTHROPIC_API_KEY, ALLOWED_DOMAINS, MAX_RUN_USD, MAX_STEPS. Ship .env.example.

Out of scope, do not build: scheduling, multi-user support, a hosted dashboard, CAPTCHA solving, proxy rotation, any attempt to evade bot detection.

Deliver a README with install steps, one worked example task, and a blunt Limitations section listing what will break.
